title: Security of Modified HFC' Encryptment
summary: The proposed modified HFC' uses injective padding under HFC's SCU security, but formal confidentiality and integrity proofs, especially for otCTXT, remain open.

formal_statement.body: For the modified HFC' encryptment scheme, which uses a second key and an authentication tag derived from the binding tag, formalize and prove confidentiality and integrity properties, in particular $\mathrm{otCTXT}$ security, when the padding is injective rather than prefix-free, relying on the underlying HFC scheme's SCU security. This remains unresolved: the intuition that successful forgery requires guessing a random authentication tag or breaking the underlying SCU security has not been formalized or proved for the modified scheme.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption security analysis for the modified HFC' encryptment scheme.
assumptions: The padding is injective rather than prefix-free.
The underlying HFC scheme satisfies SCU security.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Formalize and prove the modified scheme's confidentiality and integrity properties, particularly otCTXT security, from the stated forgery intuition and underlying SCU security.

citations.label: Fast Message Franking: From Invisible Salamanders to Encryptment

progress.summary: The source gives the intuition that a successful forgery must guess a random authentication tag or break the underlying HFC scheme's SCU security. It explicitly leaves formalizing this intuition and proving the modified scheme's properties open.
citation_labels: Yevgeniy Dodis et al., Fast Message Franking: From Invisible Salamanders to Encryptment
